perennials/5c236f1:
The app fetched three static JSON files under public/data (about 8 MB), which a
weekly GitHub Action re-pulled from Permapeople and recommitted. This moves the
dataset behind a Node and Postgres service (server/) hosted on Railway. The
service pulls the whole Permapeople database, normalizes it with a verbatim port
of scripts/data/transform.mjs, and serves plants.json, facets.json, and
meta.json. It seeds from the live data on an empty boot and refreshes weekly on
its own, so nothing has to commit a snapshot.

The client fetches those payloads from the API. Search, facets, and offline
caching are unchanged; the service worker now caches the cross-origin dataset.
The Permapeople key lives in the service environment, never in the browser or
this repo.

Removes public/data/*.json and .github/workflows/refresh-data.yml.
site/5cda9c0:
Pages serves static files and runs nothing, so there is no server to check
a password against; any gate that hides markup behind a JS comparison ships
the content anyway and loses to View Source. So /keep serves ciphertext
instead. The passphrase derives an AES-GCM key in the browser via PBKDF2 at
600k iterations, and document titles live inside the encrypted payload, so
an unopened vault does not leak what it holds. The path can stay guessable
because the encryption is the control, not the obscurity.

scripts/seal.mjs builds the vault. It prompts with echo off rather than
reading argv or the environment, keeping the passphrase out of shell
history and the process table, and it refuses anything under 12 characters
since an attacker with the file guesses offline at hardware speed.
